content.user_title: Manage Immutable Document IDs with Shirushi
content.value_statement: Document identifiers can become inconsistent when files move or change across a Git repository. Shirushi provides commands and conventions for stable IDs, references, and integrity checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to validate document IDs and index integrity with Shirushi.
Shows how to scan repository documents and retrieve metadata by document ID.
Guides assignment of identifiers to new Markdown documents.
Provides a sample configuration for enums, serial values, years, and checksums.
Documents YAML frontmatter and @see reference conventions for tracked documents.
limitations: Requires the Shirushi command-line tool to be installed separately.
Does not implement the Shirushi commands or document their installation.
Provides one example identifier format and limited configuration options.
Does not explain recovery procedures for invalid indexes or conflicting identifiers.

use_cases.title: Validate documentation changes
use_cases.description: Run integrity checks before commits or against a pull request base branch.

use_cases.title: Standardize repository documents
use_cases.description: Define consistent identifiers and frontmatter for specifications and architecture records.

use_cases.title: Enforce document references
use_cases.description: Track code references to documents and detect changes during continuous integration.

prompt_templates.title: List Shirushi documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to list all Shirushi-managed documents in a readable table.

prompt_templates.title: Assign a document ID
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me assign a Shirushi document ID to [document path] and explain the expected frontmatter.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare the Shirushi command that validates changes against [base branch] and checks document references.

prompt_templates.title: Design an identifier configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .shirushi.yml identifier format for [components] and [document types], using year, scoped serial, and checksum dimensions.

output_examples.input: How can I find the specification with ID PCE-SPEC-2025-0001-G?
output_examples.output: Use the Shirushi show command with that document ID. The result should provide the matching document information.

output_examples.input: What metadata should a managed specification include?
output: A stable doc_id matching the repository format.
A doc_type value that maps to the configured document kind.

output_examples.input: How should I validate a pull request?
output_examples.output: Run Shirushi lint against the target base branch and enable reference checking before merging.

best_practices: Run validation before commits and in continuous integration.
Treat assigned document IDs as immutable when files move or titles change.
Keep identifier dimensions and document types synchronized with repository conventions.
anti_patterns: Do not manually reuse an identifier from another document.
Do not recalculate hashes without reviewing the related content changes.
Do not merge reference failures without identifying the changed document.

faq.question: What file types does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Markdown documents with YAML frontmatter and YAML-based Shirushi configuration.

faq.question: Does the skill install Shirushi?
faq.answer: No. It assumes the Shirushi command-line tool is already available.

faq.question: Can Shirushi find a document by ID?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented show command retrieves document information for a supplied document ID.

faq.question: Can I validate only pull request changes?
faq.answer: Yes. The lint command accepts a base revision and can also check references.

faq.question: How are new IDs created?
faq.answer: The assign command adds an ID according to the repository configuration and document path.

faq.question: What happens when referenced documents change?
faq.answer: Shirushi tracks @see document references and warns when their target documents change.
